title: Global Security Briefing — Baseline Verification
bluf: China-Taiwan tensions escalated with military exercises near the median line, while Iran signaled readiness for renewed nuclear talks. NATO Baltic deployments continue.

headline_judgments.claim: China will conduct naval exercises near Taiwan within 7 days
Iran nuclear talks resume within 14 days
NATO increases Baltic forward presence by 3 battalions
Brazil fiscal consolidation passes lower house
Semiconductor export controls expanded to new categories

sections.title: Asia-Pacific Security
sections.narrative: China's People's Liberation Army conducted live-fire exercises near the Taiwan Strait median line on May 19. The exercises involved J-20 stealth fighters and Type 055 destroyers, simulating anti-access/area denial (A2/AD) operations. This represents the highest readiness posture since the 2022 Pelosi visit.

judgments.claim: PLA exercises will continue for at least 7 more days

sections.title: Middle East Nuclear Diplomacy
sections.narrative: Iran's new president signaled willingness to resume JCPOA negotiations in Vienna. IAEA inspectors report continued enrichment at 60% purity at Fordow. The window for diplomatic resolution is narrowing as Iran's nuclear latency decreases.

judgments.claim: Iran will agree to IAEA snap inspections within 30 days

sections.title: NATO Eastern Flank
sections.narrative: NATO announced deployment of 3 additional battlegroups to Poland, Estonia, and Latvia. Response to drone incursion incident in Latvia that brought down the coalition government.

judgments.claim: At least one more NATO state reports drone incursion within 7 days

sections.title: Global Finance & Markets
sections.narrative: Taiwan Strait tensions drove Kalshi KXTAIWAN contracts to 65¢. DXY strengthened on safe-haven flows. Brent crude held above 2 on Middle East risk premium.

action_lines.action: Monitor PLA Eastern Fleet satellite imagery daily

gaps.description: Exact PLA order of battle not confirmed
